articles.title: ‘Standard’ velvet hangers? There’s nothing standard about some of the items on John Lewis’s uni essentials list| Emma Beddington
articles.summary: It used to be that dorm rooms were chaotically messy. Does this new generation really need an £80 spice rack and velvet clothes hangers? Of all the questions this year’s freshers may be nervously asking themselves as they prepare for this next phase – did I pick the right course?
body: Fret no longer, enquiring young minds: John Lewis has the answer on its packing checklist for students. Thirty to 40, it claims, wildly, “consisting mostly of standard velvet or plastic hangers”. “Standard” velvet? I missed this memo.

I found the list via the student news site the Tab, which posted a TikTok mocking J-Lew’s notions of what constitute “essentials”: a £495 Marc Jacobs bag, a £399 desk and an £80 spice rack carousel (I also spotted a £185 Ralph Lauren quarter-zip for those must-attend “man in finance” costume parties).

In fairness, most of the stuff on there is fine, but the Stanley cups and shower squeegees conjure a slightly dispiriting picture of wellness-focused, sensible, hygienic youth. I know that’s their generation’s reputation, but it would be nice if parents could be persuaded not to stock up, instead letting them go rogue and fill their kitchens, bathrooms and bedrooms with chaotically impractical stuff they choose themselves. Isn’t that what early adulthood is all about?

Does this new generation really need an £80 spice rack and velvet clothes hangers?

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Ernie the danger dog – who loves dicing with death
articles.summary: He has chased a deer across a dual carriageway, eaten an entire tray of chocolate brownies and jumped head first into a canal. But despite all the worry he brings us, he is extraordinarily lovable.
body: Ernie found his way into our hearts and home about nine years ago, when he strategically crawled into my lap during a family visit to meet a litter of puppies. While all the other beagle puppies ran wild, Ernie sat comfortably on me with his long, soft ears dangling down. We chose him because of his placid nature and named him Ernie after my mum’s late dad, who coincidentally also had short legs and a bit of a round belly.
After a few weeks we realised that Ernie was anything but placid. His gentle temperament quickly morphed into an unruly and persistent need to find his way into danger.

The most shocking incident happened one morning in November 2022. Ernie spotted a deer in the forest behind our house. He darted away from me and my mum, through the forest and towards a busy dual carriageway. Ignoring our screams, Ernie crossed the road, missing multiple lorries and cars, making his way to safety on a small patch of grass on the pavement. It was a miracle he had managed to avoid injury.

articles.title: ‘It’s absolutely criminal’: US tipping culture has reached the UK – and is causing chaos
articles.summary: Service charges used to be a matter of choice, but now consumers feel obliged to pay them for even a cup of coffee. How do we navigate this minefield and who is really profiting? In a London pub, Greg Double was brutally confronted with the reality of Britain’s evolving tipping culture.
body: Tipping was awkward enough in the UK when the general rule was 10% at a restaurant, plus anxiety about whether you should tip the hairdresser, babysitter or food-delivery driver. Now, with tipping suggested ever more frequently, US-style, it has become a minefield to Britons. The amounts edge higher – in fancier London restaurants, a 15% service charge is relatively commonplace. And it’s often asked for – in coffee shops for example, when you pay – before any service is delivered.

Tipping may be a social behaviour, but politics and economics also inform it. Since October 2024, all service charges and tips in Great Britain must go to staff, which boosts low salaries. Hospitality businesses, struggling with the rises in minimum wage and national insurance, are surely happy that it’s tipping customers who are supplementing wages, rather than themselves. As the news site London Centric pointed out recently in an article headlined “ How American tipping culture came to London ”, adding an “optional” service charge avoids tax, puts more money in the pockets of staff and means businesses don’t have to raise prices, which puts off customers.

articles.title: Georgina Hayden’s quick and easy recipe for charred corn, jalapeño and black bean nachos | Quick and easy
articles.summary: A fun and easily customisable snack, to be enjoyed by kids and adults alike. Corn is a late-summer staple in our house, but its arrival often leaves me feeling a little blue (end of summer and all that). So, instead, I like to entertain more and make the most of the warm, light evenings.
body: Put a large frying pan on a high heat, add the corn and fry for five to 10 minutes, until the kernels start to char. Transfer to a large bowl.

Pour the vegetable oil into the pan, then add the black beans and ground cumin, and season well. Fry on a high heat for about five minutes, until the beans start to crisp up and pop a little, then tip into the bowl of charred corn.

Finely grate in the zest of one of the limes, and squeeze in the juice of one and a half limes. Add most of the chopped coriander and chilli, then toss well. Tweak and adjust the seasoning to taste, adding more lime juice or salt as required.

Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Spread out the tortilla chips on a baking sheet or tray, and cover with both grated cheeses. Pop under the grill for a couple of minutes, until the cheese turns oozy – if if starts to catch, turn off the heat and leave it to finish melting in the residual heat.
points: A fun and easily customisable snack, to be enjoyed by kids and adults alike.

articles.title: The 26 Best Airbnbs in Milan, From Industrial Lofts to Charming Studios
articles.summary: On your next visit to Italy’s fashion capital, skip the hotel and stay in one of the best Airbnbs in Milan instead. Vogue rounds up its favorites.
body: The fashion, the architecture, the design, the risotto: Whatever brought you to Milan, there’s a good chance it’ll hook you long enough to plan a return trip before you’ve even checked out. More modern than Rome, more fast-paced than Florence, this industrial city is a hub for the country’s fashion and financial elite alike. Now, with Milan Fashion Week (and Vogue World 2026 ) just around the corner in September, there’s even more incentive to visit. And while you could always book a stay at a sleek hotel, a Milanese Airbnb offers up the chance to slow down, make yourself at home, and get a taste of life as a local.

Much like the cosmopolitan city itself, the best Airbnbs in Milan cover a lot of ground in style. There’s a painter’s attic nestled among the rooftops, where stained glass and wood beam ceilings make you feel like you’re stepping back in time. There’s an industrial duplex that leans into the contemporary edge of the newer parts of city. There’s even a bohemian top-floor apartment, where overgrown greens and a glass ceiling give it the look of a grown-up treehouse. Each of these vacation rentals has its own charm.
points: On your next visit to Italy’s fashion capital, skip the hotel and stay in one of the best Airbnbs in Milan instead.

articles.title: The Best Dining Is Happening During the Day
articles.summary: A Japanese bakery in Nashville, cult breakfast burritos in Brooklyn, Indigenous fry bread in Portland: These are the seven best new daytime spots in the US.
body: The majority of restaurant scouting happens at night; many of our Best New Restaurants list are only open for dinner service. Lucky for us, a few operate daily daytime hours (like Agnes and Sherman in Houston and The Wayland Mill in Seattle), or lunch or brunch service on the weekends (like Broken Spanish Comedor in L.A.), but these are the exceptions for the myriad restaurants that make our scouting long list.

Rather than filling up on random meals throughout the day, we are instead on the hunt for exciting eateries serving food outside dinner hours—and bonus points if they are new. Restaurants continue to approach daytime service with more intention and creativity than ever, but this is not a new trend; we reported on this last year with our list of the 14 spots waking up the breakfast menu. But our scouting team of editors observed that this year, hospitality pros are not phoning it in at lunch, happy hour, or even that late afternoon slump.

articles.title: 20 Modern Jewelry Brands Worth Knowing in 2026
articles.summary: Get to know the modern jewelry brands Vogue editors are loving. From Juju Vera to Vertigo to Dezso, these designers deserve a spot in your jewelry box.
body: The best contemporary jewelry brands are sometimes the hardest to discover. Many people are familiar with the biggest and most dazzling names in jewelry—Cartier, Tiffany, Van Cleef & Arpels—and know where to look for the independent labels that do great everyday basics, but sometimes, it can be difficult to find cool contemporary jewelry brands that are making fun, fresh pieces not everyone else is going to have.

The basics—a good hoop earring and a dainty gold chain —are great starting points when starting a jewelry collection, but as you begin to build out a more robust assortment, you’ll likely find yourself looking for something unique to help round out your collection.

And while the list of designers who are catching our eyes here at Vogue far exceeds this list, let me introduce you to some of the buzziest names (and their designs) in today’s contemporary jewelry world—a fresh crop of designers well deserving of a coveted spot in your jewelry box. From Juju Vera’s sculpted treasures to Charlotte Chesnais’s winding creations and Dezso’s shell-laden necklaces, you’re sure to find something (maybe even, a few somethings) suited to your style.

articles.title: Gooey Butter Cookies
articles.summary: These playful cookies are reminiscent of St. Louis butter cake, with specks of crunchy rice brittle throughout.
body: Cook ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar, 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter, and 1 Tbsp. water in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the color of honey and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and, working quickly, add ¾ cup Rice Krispies or other puffed rice cereal and mix until evenly coated. Add ¼ tsp. baking soda and ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt and stir just until mixture puffs and slightly lightens in color.

Immediately scrape mixture out onto a rimmed baking sheet lined with a nonstick baking mat (or you can use parchment paper lightly coated with nonstick vegetable oil spray ), pushing as needed to work into a single layer; sprinkle with flaky sea salt. Let brittle cool (it will harden), then coarsely chop into about ½" pieces.

articles.title: Just Browsing: L’Agence Fuses California Ease With a French Edge on Madison Avenue
articles.summary: From standout denim to elegant slip dresses, these are the best pieces to shop at L’Agence’s flagship.
body: In the heart of the Upper East Side, L’Agence is bringing California ease matched with a little je ne sais quoi to New York City. Sitting just off the corner of 75th Street on Madison Avenue, its flagship houses their full offering, including newly launched fall styles. I got the chance to visit the store early in the morning, before opening—with a coffee in hand and the racks perfectly untouched—and browse denim, jackets, and, of course, the label’s statement occasion wear. I was ready to try on a little bit of everything.

The brand has been known for the cult-favorite denim styles since their launch in 2008, so naturally it was the first rack I ran to. I was drawn to the Clayton, Scottie, and Rosalyn—each offering a distinct silhouette, ready for daily wear, whether that means a day at the office or a long Saturday stroll. But denim was just the start. Classic tees for effortless layering, elegant slips for summer’s heat, statement skirts for a touch of drama, and playful outerwear for the season ahead. It’s the kind of assortment that builds out a well-rounded wardrobe, not just filling in the gaps.
points: From standout denim to elegant slip dresses, these are the best pieces to shop at L’Agence’s flagship.
